scholars: Ibn Kathir says this surah is linked to Surah Al-Fil, the one before it. Allah stopped the elephant army and destroyed it, so the Quraysh could stay together safely in their city. (Muhammad ibn Ishaq and Abdur-Rahman ibn Zayd said this.) The word 'ilaf' means joining them together.
Ibn Jarir (At-Tabari) said the first word shows wonder: be amazed at how Allah brought the Quraysh together and was so kind to them.
The book Tanwir al-Miqbas (from Ibn Abbas) says it means: tell the Quraysh to believe that Allah is One.

Ibn Kathir explains: every winter they traveled to Yemen, and every summer they traveled to Ash-Sham, to trade. They came back safe, because people respected them as the people who lived near Allah's holy place. Even people who traveled with them were safe.
The book Al-Jalalayn says they made these two trips every year to get things to sell, and they were proud to take care of the House of Allah.
Ibn Kathir explains: Allah tells them to say thank you for this big favor. Worship Him alone, just like He gave them a safe holy place and a Holy House.
The book Tanwir al-Miqbas says: let the Quraysh say that Allah is One, the Lord of the Kaaba.

Ibn Kathir explains: Allah feeds them when they are hungry and keeps them safe from fear. So they should worship Him alone and not idols. Whoever listens, Allah gives safety in this life and the next. Whoever does not listen, Allah takes both away. (Ibn Kathir also shows Surah An-Nahl, 16:112–113, about a safe town that said no to Allah's favors, so Allah made it taste hunger and fear.)
The book Al-Jalalayn says they were hungry in Makkah because there were few crops, and they feared the army of the elephant.
The book Tanwir al-Miqbas says Allah fed them after a hunger that some say lasted seven years, and made them safe from fear of the enemy.
